# Rome 46 BC – Mathematics & measurement

K = knowledge level · use = none/wrong/partial/correct · make = producibility with local means · accept = acceptance.

- **Zero and positional notation** [`zero_place_value`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/zero_place_value.md) — K1, use none, make easy, accept medium. Numerals are additive; an empty column on the counting board is the only 'nothing', never written. Nihil is no number. Philosophers will ask how nothing can be a quantity. Local: bankers (argentarii) in the Forum; clerks of the tax companies (publicani); public scribes of the treasury (aerarium). Elsewhere: Babylon (Parthian): astronomer-scribes write base-60 place value with a placeholder sign for an empty place; Alexandria and Rhodes: Greek astronomers compute in Babylonian sixtieths; Han China: counting rods, decimal place value with a blank for zero.
- **Hindu-Arabic numerals and written arithmetic** [`arabic_numerals`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/arabic_numerals.md) — K0, use none, make easy, accept medium. Sums are done with pebbles and on the fingers, then recorded in letters. Written column arithmetic works on wax tablets; bookkeepers and tax farmers gain, and fear forgery. Local: wax tablets and stylus, erasable, ideal for written sums; household ledgers (codex accepti et expensi).
- **Abacus and counting board** [`abacus_counting_board`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/abacus_counting_board.md) — K4, use correct, make easy, accept high. Pebbles (calculi) on a board ruled in columns for I, X, C, M, with fives between and twelfths beside; finger signs too. The bronze bead abacus is not yet attested. Local: schoolmasters who drill reckoning (calculatores); bankers' tables in the Forum.
- **Common fractions and the rule of three** [`fractions_rule_of_three`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/fractions_rule_of_three.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept high. Fractions are twelfths of the as (unciae) and their parts, drilled in school; Greek reckoners use unit fractions, astronomers sixtieths. A general numerator-over-denominator notation is missing.
- **Decimal fractions** [`decimal_fractions`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/decimal_fractions.md) — K0, use none, make easy, accept low. Needs place value first. Money, weights and inheritances run in twelfths, which divide by three and four; tenths look clumsier to a Roman.
- **Negative numbers** [`negative_numbers`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/negative_numbers.md) — K0, use none, make easy, accept low. Receipts and outlays stand in separate columns of the ledger. A number less than nothing is absurd; calling it a debt helps. Elsewhere: Han China: red and black counting rods for gain and loss (written up by the 1st c. AD).
- **Square roots and irrational numbers** [`square_roots_irrationals`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/square_roots_irrationals.md) — K2, use partial, make medium, accept medium. Incommensurable lengths are classified in Euclid, book 10. Surveyors and architects use rough rules. Digit-by-digit root extraction needs place value.
- **Logarithms** [`logarithms`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/logarithms.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept medium. Needs place value and decimal fractions, then months of table work by trained reckoners. Astronomers in Alexandria gain most.
- **Slide rule** [`slide_rule`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/slide_rule.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept low
- **Symbolic algebra** [`symbolic_algebra`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/symbolic_algebra.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept low. Problems are stated and solved in words or as geometry. Greek letters already serve as numerals, which makes letters for unknowns confusing.
- **Solving quadratic and cubic equations** [`quadratic_cubic_equations`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/quadratic_cubic_equations.md) — K2, use partial, make medium, accept low. Quadratics are solved as geometry (application of areas, Euclid II and VI). Doubling the cube is done with curves and instruments such as Eratosthenes' mesolabe, not by formula.
- **Systems of linear equations (elimination and matrices)** [`linear_equations_matrices`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/linear_equations_matrices.md) — K1, use partial, make medium, accept low. One-unknown problems are solved by trial values in the Egyptian manner. Systematic elimination for several unknowns is unknown here. Elsewhere: Han China: elimination on the counting board (in the Nine Chapters by the 1st c. AD).
- **Complex numbers** [`complex_numbers`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/complex_numbers.md) — K0, use none, make very-hard, accept low
- **Prime numbers and number theory** [`prime_numbers_number_theory`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/prime_numbers_number_theory.md) — K2, use correct, make easy, accept low. Euclid VII-IX and Eratosthenes' sieve exist in Greek. Roman Pythagoreans care for the lore of perfect and friendly numbers; nobody sees a use.
- **Combinatorics (permutations, combinations, Pascal's triangle)** [`combinatorics_permutations`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/combinatorics_permutations.md) — K1, use partial, make easy, accept low. Chrysippus claimed over a million compound statements from ten simple ones; Hipparchus disputed it with his own counts. No general rules, no triangle of coefficients.
- **Compound interest and exponential growth** [`compound_interest_exponential_growth`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/compound_interest_exponential_growth.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Interest runs by the month; 1 per cent monthly (centesima) is the ceiling. In 50 BC Cicero fought Brutus' agents over a Salamis loan at 48 per cent. No tables. Local: Titus Pomponius Atticus, financier; bankers (argentarii) in the Forum; the debt crisis and Caesar's debt-relief measures of 49-47 BC.
- **Deductive geometry and proof (Euclid, Pythagoras)** [`geometry_proof`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/geometry_proof.md) — K2, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Euclid, Archimedes and Apollonius are read in Greek by a few. Cicero's judgement: Romans confine geometry to measuring and reckoning. No Latin Euclid exists. Local: Greek tutors and libraries in great houses; Varro, charged by Caesar with organising a public library. Elsewhere: Alexandria: Museum and Library; Rhodes and Athens: schools.
- **Pi and the measurement of the circle** [`pi_circle_measurement`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/pi_circle_measurement.md) — K2, use partial, make easy, accept high. Archimedes' bounds 223/71 and 22/7 stand in his Measurement of a Circle. Craftsmen use 3 or 3 1/8; wheelwrights, pipe makers and vault builders would take a better rule.
- **Trigonometry** [`trigonometry`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/trigonometry.md) — K2, use partial, make hard, accept medium. Hipparchus' table of chords belongs to Greek astronomy; nobody in Rome computes with it. Sines and a dense table are months of work and want place-value arithmetic. Elsewhere: Alexandria and Rhodes: astronomers using Hipparchus' chords.
- **Coordinate geometry and graphs of functions** [`coordinate_geometry`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/coordinate_geometry.md) — K1, use partial, make medium, accept low. Astronomers fix stars and geographers places by two numbers; surveyors lay land on a grid from cardo and decumanus. Plotting a curve from an equation is unknown.
- **Non-Euclidean geometry** [`non_euclidean_geometry`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/non_euclidean_geometry.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept low. Euclid's parallel postulate is already felt to want a proof (Posidonius redefined parallels as equidistant). Geometry on the sphere is not seen as a rival geometry.
- **Linear perspective and technical drawing** [`perspective_technical_drawing`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/perspective_technical_drawing.md) — K3, use partial, make medium, accept medium. Wall painters of the current fashion open walls into deep colonnades with roughly converging lines, no single vanishing point. Architects draw plans and elevations; scaled machine drawings are rare. Local: Second Style wall paintings in houses on the Palatine and in the villas around Vesuvius.
- **Surveying, levelling and triangulation** [`surveying_triangulation`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/surveying_triangulation.md) — K4, use partial, make easy, accept high. Surveyors lay out roads, camps and colony grids with groma and rods and level aqueducts with water levels; Caesar is settling veterans now. Angles are not measured; no triangulation. Local: land surveyors (mensores) for Caesar's veteran colonies; army camp surveyors. Elsewhere: Greek astronomers' sighting tube and dioptra.
- **Solar calendar with leap years** [`solar_calendar_leap_years`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/solar_calendar_leap_years.md) — K3, use partial, make easy, accept medium. Happening now: 46 BC runs 445 days. The new year of 365 1/4 days is 11 minutes too long, a day in 128 years; Hipparchus' shorter value is ignored. Local: Caesar, pontifex maximus, who issues the edict; Sosigenes, his astronomer (Pliny); Marcus Flavius, scribe named by Macrobius; college of pontiffs, who lose control of intercalation. Elsewhere: Egypt: 365-day civil year with no leap day; the Canopus decree of 238 BC ordering one was ignored; Babylon: 19-year cycle of intercalary months.
- **Decimal, coherent system of units (metric system)** [`metric_system_units`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/metric_system_units.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept low. Foot, pound and amphora are standard in Roman territory, divided in twelfths; the amphora is defined as a cubic foot. Decimal units want decimal numerals and a dictator's fiat. Local: standard weights and measures on the Capitol.
- **Probability and statistics** [`probability_statistics`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/probability_statistics.md) — K0, use none, make easy, accept low. Dice and knucklebones are everywhere, but the outcome is Fortuna's, and lots are drawn to learn the gods' will. Census rolls, grain-dole lists and sea loans offer data. Local: Caesar's street-by-street recount of grain recipients in 46 BC (320,000 cut to 150,000); lenders of sea loans (faenus nauticum).
- **Bayes' theorem (updating belief by evidence)** [`bayes_theorem`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/bayes_theorem.md) — K0, use none, make medium, accept low
- **Errors of measurement, the bell curve and least squares** [`normal_distribution_errors`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/normal_distribution_errors.md) — K0, use none, make hard, accept low. Astronomers pick the one observation they trust. Averaging repeated measurements is new and easy; the theory behind it needs probability and calculus.
- **Graphs of data (line, bar and pie charts)** [`data_graphs`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/data_graphs.md) — K0, use none, make easy, accept medium. Records are lists on wax tablets, papyrus rolls and whitened notice boards. Grain prices or Tiber levels drawn as a line over time would be new.
- **Calculus (differentiation and integration)** [`calculus`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/calculus.md) — K1, use none, make very-hard, accept low. Archimedes' exhaustion proofs and his Method (weighing thin slices) exist in Greek, read by a handful. No algebra, coordinates or place-value numbers to build on.
- **Infinite series and the number e** [`infinite_series_e`](https://blueprintsfromtomorrow.com/techtree/generated/tech/infinite_series_e.md) — K1, use none, make hard, accept low. Zeno's paradoxes are a school topic; Archimedes summed 1 + 1/4 + 1/16 and so on in his Quadrature of the Parabola. No general notion of a series.
